thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Set For Third Straight Down Day As Tech Shares Tumble Again

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Set For Third Straight Down Day As Tech Shares Tumble Again
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Google parent Alphabet set for fifth straight negative session
U.S. stocks fell on Thursday, with major indexes shedding a slight early gain to turn solidly lower as technology stocks once again weighed on the broader market.
The decline builds on a similarly sharp decline on Wednesday, which was also fueled by tech losses.
How are benchmarks performing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 57 points, or 0.2%, to 25,913. The S&P 500 index shed 17 points to 2,872, a drop of 0.6%. The Nasdaq Composite Index shed 84 points to 7,911, a drop of 1.1%. Both the S&P and the Nasdaq were on track for their third straight daily drop, while the Nasdaq was also poised for its weekly percentage loss since March.
The technology sector was the weakest performer of the day, falling 1.3%. On Wednesday, it slumped 1.5% in the industry's biggest daily drop since July 30. The sector is on track for its biggest weekly loss since March.
What's driving the market?
As on Wednesday's session, there was no obvious catalyst for the drop in tech, which has been the strongest-performing sector of the year by far. The length and scale of the "momentum" trade has resulted in many analysts saying the move has been overdone.
Among notable decliners, Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell 2% in its biggest one-day drop since April. Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) was down 2.6%, also its biggest one-day drop since April, as well as its fifth straight negative session.
Facebook Inc. (FB) fell 3% in its fourth straight daily decline, dropping to its lowest level since April.
"This is very much a tech-centric reversion. It is long overdue, given how much the Nasdaq has been outperforming the rest of the market," said Peter Kenny, a market strategist who is currently the president of Kenny & Co. "This is bigger than FAANG, but the scale of that move is the primary driver of what we're seeing today and what we saw yesterday. I think there's still some downside ahead, and that this won't be a short-term correction, but something that will take a long time to work through."
FAANG is an acronym that refers to a quintet of large-capitalization technology and internet stocks that have sharply outperformed the broader market over the past several years.
The tech weakness overshadowed some economic data. In the latest readings on the labor market, the U.S. created 163,000 private-sector jobs in August (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/adp-us-creates-163000-private-sector-jobs-in-august-2018-09-06-81031928), according to payrolls processor ADP. This was below the 182,000 that had been expected, as well as down from July's 217,000 reading. Separately, jobless claims fell to their lowest level since 1969.
The reports come a day before the August payroll report, which is expected to show 200,000 jobs added last month.
Meanwhile, the U.S. and Canada continued high-stakes negotiations in the effort to revamp the North American Free Trade Agreement, which President Donald Trump has indicated he is prepared to move forward with Mexico and without its northern neighbor.
Those trade tensions come amid the start of a public comment on the Trump administration's plan to impose tariffs on an additional $200 billion of Chinese goods. Reports indicated that President Donald Trump could impose the tariffs as soon as this week.
Fears about the impact of a strengthening dollar on emerging economies also remained a key concerns for industry participants, worried about the possibility of risk factors that could more definitively hit investor sentiment.

What data and Fed speakers are ahead?
In addition to the labor-market data, growth in U.S. productivity (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/second-quarter-us-productivity-growth-stays-at-29-2018-09-06) in the second quarter was left unchanged at 2.9% after the government's latest update.
Two reads on the services sector painted a mixed picture. The Institute for Supply Management's August read on the services sector rose to 58.5% from 55.7% in the previous month, while the final IHS Markit reading on the services purchasing managers index fell to 54.8 in August from 56 in July. Separately, a read on factory orders fell 0.8% in July.
New York Federal Reserve President John Williams is on tap to deliver a speech at 10 a.m. about the regional and national economy at the University of Buffalo School of Management.
Which stocks are in focus?
G-III ApparelGroup Ltd. shares (GIII) rose 3% the owner or licensee of brands including DKNY, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger among others, blew past earnings estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dkny-parent-g-iii-apparel-shares-soar-7-premarket-after-blowout-earnings-2018-09-06) for its fiscal second quarter.
BioCryst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (BCRX) fell 0.8% after it said it had won a $35 million, five-year contract (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/biocryst-stock-surges-6-premarket-after-winning-35-million-cdc-contract-for-flu-therapy-2018-09-06) from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for up to 50,000 doses of its antiviral flu therapy Rapivab.
Lands' End Inc.' shares (LE) plunged 13% after the clothing, accessories and home products retailer reported a wider second-quarter loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lands-ends-stock-tumbles-after-wider-loss-same-store-sales-decline-2018-09-06) and declines in same-store sales.
Navistar International Corp. (NAV) shares fell 3% after it reported third-quarter results that beat expectations. It also raised its full-year revenue outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/navistars-stock-rallies-after-earnings-beat-upbeat-outlook-2018-09-06).
Barnes & Noble Inc. (BKS) reported first-quarter results that included a wider net loss than the previous year, a fall in revenue, and a drop of 6.1% in its same-store sales. Shares fell 6%.
What other assets were in focus?
Asian stock markets closed broadly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-though-nikkei-sags-again-2018-09-05) Thursday after a tech selloff on Wall Street.
Japan's Nikkei fell 0.4%, the Shanghai Composite finished the session 0.5% lower, while the Shenzhen Composite Index closed off 0.7%.
